title: An Otherworldly Romantic Comedy
text: “No, wait, why are you asking me!?”
That’s because it’s basically the same as a Filolial-sama, I say.
“I’ll let him handle that troublesome bird over there and answer this one myself, I think.”
“Right. Good to see you make yourself useful for once, Motoyasu.”
Father had gone and praised me. This mission, I simply had to see it through.
“Well then, Ho-kun, do tell me, I say!”
Even as I thought that, I supposed I ought to keep half an ear turned toward Father’s side of things.
“You’ve got no intention of actually listening, do you! Fine, fine. If you’re still curious after we finish over here, I’ll tell you then.”
“Right, let’s get into it, shall we? I’ll tell you about a world I stopped by and stayed in a while back—one where I worked as a dormitory matron.”

And so Arc began telling us about a world he’d stayed in during his travels. Apparently its level of civilization was similar to this world’s. According to him, there had once been a great conflict there, and though a fair amount of time had passed since then and peace had technically settled in, the various nations were still locked in a tense standoff, glaring at one another. Amid all that, the nations had jointly established a school, ostensibly for the sake of fostering friendship, sharing technology, and educating the next generation. Arc had apparently infiltrated that world in order to exterminate some particularly nasty troublemakers. If he’d simply used his full power, he could have flushed them out and dealt with them easily enough, but it was the sort of delicate situation where doing so risked breaking the world itself. So Arc had asked a local dragon for help and slipped in disguised as the dormitory matron of the school in question.
“Why a dorm matron, though? I mean, uh, Arc, you don’t exactly look old enough for that kind of job.”
Arc looked something like a cat beastman to me, though I couldn’t really say much about their age. Still, there was a certain air about them that suggested they’d lived quite a long time.
“Well, you see, if I enrolled as a student, I’d have had to sit through classes and all sorts of things, and that would’ve eaten up too much time.”
“Huh… but being a dorm matron sounds like a pretty busy job too, doesn’t it?”
“It’s a lot quicker than sitting through lessons, trust me.”
Ah, I could tell at once—this was the swift, efficient work of a true veteran, I say. After all, watching Father cook in the kitchen made that sort of thing easy enough to believe.
“Well, in the end I got roped into teaching classes too, though.”
“Sounds like putting the cart before the horse.”
“Ahaha… I mean, I did have some experience teaching, so it worked out. I just taught what I knew, within the bounds of that world’s natural laws.”
“Hoh… and what exactly are you good at?”
“Hmm… I’d say I’m fairly well-versed in alchemy and magical theory. Lots of things, really.”
Father glanced over toward the direction of Doctor’s research lab. No doubt he was considering whether it might be worth having Arc explain a thing or two, given the expertise.

“Well, if I stop here, it just sounds like I was some random dorm matron, so let me get into the details. So, this school—once it was founded, students and the sons and daughters of nobility from various countries gathered there a little before classes even started, and before long, a rather unusual nightly event began taking place.”
“An unusual event, you say?”
Big Sister asked.

“Yeah. See, the school had this issue where the facilities in the boys’ and girls’ dormitories ended up wildly unequal due to some sloppy management on the administration’s part. The boys’ dorm was basically falling apart, and using that as justification, one particular boy boldly declared war on the girls—announcing he’d peep on them out of sheer principle. Naturally, other boys rallied to his side, and the girls rose to meet the challenge, and thus began a sort of rule-based mock war.”

Apparently the reasoning was something like ‘well, the boys’ dorm is a wreck, so let this much slide,’ and somehow that flew, and every single night became a lively battlefield of attack and defense. Arc said this all with such heartfelt nostalgia that everyone present ended up looking utterly exasperated. And then, for some reason, Father turned and stared straight at me.

“Sounds like something out of an old manga from two generations back… I genuinely can’t comprehend how a situation like that comes about, but setting that aside—I suppose there really are perverts who love peeping no matter what world you’re in.”
“I can kind of understand the pursuit of romance, though!”
Ho-kun was nodding along in agreement with that sort of talk.
“If it is Filolial-sama’s wish, then I too shall throw myself into the peeping campaign with everything I have, I say!”
What a delightfully fun-sounding place, I say!

“Yeah. Because of all that, it doubled as practical combat training too. There were students who were baffled, like ‘I never imagined I’d end up teaching magic to a classmate,’ but in the end, real results came out of it. And I was the dorm matron of that very boys’ dormitory, you see.”
“A war fought over peeping, huh…”
At this point, Tiger Girl emerged from Father’s shield.
“What a truly splendid battle. I too shall wage war against Raphtalia-san, in order to bathe in the hot springs together with Naofumi-sama.”
“I feel like your choice of opponent is a bit off there.”
“Ooh, sounds kind of fun—if it’s fine for the girls to go peep on the boys too, then Big Sister’s happy to lend a hand~”
“Please don’t.”
“…So even here, similar skirmishes exist, hm. I suppose telling stories about that kind of school could indeed be amusing, but…”

“And amid all that fighting, there was actually a time when I got invited to serve as bait in the girls’ bathhouse, set up to lie in wait for the boy in question. Apparently some ordinary girl students wanted help so they could bathe safely.”
“Hm? How does that even work?”

“Sounds like it was bait meant to make it look like someone was already inside, you know? The boy in question was truly elusive—here, there, everywhere—so they placed me in one of the many hot springs, buried deep within layers of decoys.”
“So they wanted to see the look on his face when he realized it was just a cat taking a bath instead—like, ‘aw, what a letdown’!”
Ho-kun gave a thumbs up.

“I think that’s probably it, yeah? The boy in question made this utterly betrayed face, and right after that, I loudly announced to the entire student body that I was in there, and then both boys and girls came flocking over.”
“Ohh, quite the popular one, aren’t you.”
“Why, though?”
“Apparently everyone wanted to bathe with me. Got called the healing mascot of the boys’ dormitory or something.”
Looking at Arc now, I found it hard to believe such a thing, but there was no denying Arc did seem to occupy some kind of mascot position.
“Ahh… so you were the healing mascot type, huh, you.”
“I certainly never intended to be, personally.”
“Still… hmm, come to think of it, perhaps selling the rights to bathe together with Filo could be an option too…”

What did he just say!? Bathing together with Filo-tan!? I was well aware that Father and Filo-tan occasionally shared the same hot spring, but if such rights could actually be purchased, then I, Motoyasu, would obtain them by any means necessary, I say! My resolve on this matter shall not waver! Filo-tan!
“Nooo! Something about that gives me the creeps! Master! I don’t want that!”
Filo-tan, who had been eating a little ways off from Ho-kun and me, ran crying to Father.
“Hmm… no good, then. In that case, would Keel do instead?”
“Why does it come to that, big bro!? Who’d even be happy bathing with me!?”
“Well, plenty of devoted fans—men, women, children, doesn’t matter—would surely love bathing with Keel, taking turns scrubbing every inch of you.”
“Piyo!”
Luna-chan, perched atop Keel’s head, cheerfully announced her presence. It seemed Luna-chan was determined to buy up all the rights herself.
“What good does scrubbing me even do!? Once is plenty!”
“That’s where the whole ‘taking turns’ thing comes in. There’s no shortage of folks who’d want to fawn over an adorable little pup like you. Yeah. Not a bad idea at all.”
“I don’t want it! I don’t want to be washed in turns like that either!”
Keel seized the moment to firmly refuse as well.
“How should I put this… I think I understand exactly why everyone came flocking, just by using Filo and Keel-kun as examples.”
“Yeah.”
“By the way, the boy in question was actually an incredibly gifted student. You can’t really pull off something like that without genuine skill.”
Skill conquers all, indeed. Certainly, back in Japan, I too had pulled off my fair share of outrageous stunts through sheer force of will, more times than I could count.
“However you slice it, he sounds like an unrepeatable degenerate pervert. Kind of like a certain Love Hunter’s past self.”
“Well, when he needed to get serious, he really did, so he was quite popular, that guy.”
“Probably good-looking too, I bet…”
Hmm… I had a feeling that fellow and I might actually get along rather well. Provided, of course, he could truly appreciate a Filolial-sama, rather than mere pigs.
“He had all sorts of circumstances of his own too, you know. His little sister was suffering from a severe illness… no, wait, a curse, and he was working hard to break it.”
“Sounds like something you could’ve solved in an instant.”

“It wasn’t really a problem that needed me stepping in. I just heard him out, introduced him to someone I’d met in that world, and it got resolved that way. After that, he actually studied pretty seriously. Though the peeping never did stop.”
And so Arc went on, telling us tales of those school days.
Truly, a chaotic old-fashioned rom-com of a sort that could never fly with today’s public opinion, wouldn’t you say.
